```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", error = FALSE)
library(readfiscalau)
```

`readfiscalau` supports a reviewable workflow for discovering, preserving, and
validating official Australian Budget archive material. The archive API is
separate from the release readers: it captures official index evidence,
discovers direct document candidates, admits selected bytes into a durable
content-addressed store, and validates the inventory and explicit gap ledger.
Use the release readers when you need parsed fiscal data; the archive catalogue
records discovery and preservation evidence, while parseability is established
separately by each typed reader.

## Inspect the bundled catalogue first

The installed package carries a small machine-readable catalogue and captured
index snapshots. Reading and filtering it is local and safe:

```{r catalogue}
catalogue <- read_au_budget_archive_catalogue()
lapply(catalogue, function(x) if (is.data.frame(x)) dim(x) else length(x))
```

```{r candidates}
head(list_au_budget_archive_candidates(
  budget_vintage = "2025-26",
  availability = "available"
)[, c("budget_vintage", "title", "document_role",
      "source_url", "availability")])
```

The bundled candidate inventory spans the advertised official Budget range from
1901–02 through 2026–27. Its 70 captured index snapshots begin at 1926–27, so
the snapshot count should not be read as 70 snapshots covering every year from
1901–02. This is discovery evidence, not a copy of the approximately 2.33 GiB
corpus of document bytes. Missing years, broken links, insecure links, and
failed signatures remain explicit gap rows.

The durable archive location is separate from the bounded response cache:

```{r locations}
cache_path <- readfiscalau_default_cache()
archive_path <- readfiscalau_default_archive_dir()
c(
  cache = basename(cache_path),
  archive = basename(archive_path),
  distinct = !identical(cache_path, archive_path)
)
```

Set `READFISCALAU_BUDGET_ARCHIVE_DIR` when an operator needs a shared or
dedicated data volume. Do not point it at the package checkout in production.

## The explicit preservation workflow

The workflow has four distinct steps:

1. `crawl_au_budget_archive()` fetches the official root/year indexes and
   returns `documents`, `indexes`, `gaps`, and `root_entries`. Candidate
   document bytes are fetched only in the explicit admission step below.
2. `list_au_budget_archive_candidates()` or the crawl result is reviewed and
   filtered by vintage, role, availability, or revision status.
3. `archive_au_budget_documents()` admits only those explicit candidates. It
   stages one document at a time, checks size/media/signature, hashes the exact
   bytes, atomically writes the object, and checkpoints inventory/gap ledgers.
4. `validate_au_budget_archive()` checks local object hashes/sizes and accounts
   for each discovered URL through inventory or a durable gap.

The large, networked and stateful step is illustrated below rather than run
during vignette builds. Run it after reviewing the candidates and ensuring
enough free space for the advertised bytes plus the default 512 MiB reserve:

```r
discovery <- crawl_au_budget_archive()
selected <- discovery$documents[
  discovery$documents$budget_vintage == "2025-26", , drop = FALSE
]
admitted <- archive_au_budget_documents(
  candidates = selected,
  archive_dir = readfiscalau_default_archive_dir(),
  continue_on_error = TRUE,
  progress = TRUE
)
validation <- validate_au_budget_archive(
  archive_dir = readfiscalau_default_archive_dir(),
  discovery = discovery,
  archive = list(inventory = admitted)
)
```

An archive is append-only and preserves replacements as separate attributable
objects. `list_au_budget_archive()` exposes the immutable ledger; it does not
collapse replacement vintages into one “latest” row.

## Scope, provenance, and limits

Each admitted row retains source/index URLs, retrieval time, media type, hash,
terms URL, licence, attribution, and revision linkage. A locally stored object
does not expand its source licence or imply publisher endorsement. Consult
`inst/TERMS.md` for the source-level notices.

Archive validation can be complete with respect to the accounted catalogue
while still retaining explicit gaps for unavailable official links. Treat
`gaps` as part of the result, not as an implementation detail.
